what_its_for: Ergoloid mesylates is used to help with certain symptoms in older adults who have trouble with memory, confusion, mood changes, or difficulty with daily activities. It may help improve mental alertness and overall well-being. Doctors may prescribe it for age-related decline in mental function, though it is not a cure for Alzheimer's disease or dementia.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth exactly as your doctor tells you. It comes as a tablet or liquid. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water. If you are using the liquid form, measure the dose carefully with the measuring dropper that comes with the medicine. You may take it with or without food, but taking it with food may help if it upsets your stomach. Do not crush, chew, or break the tablets unless your doctor says it is okay.
dosing: The usual adult dose is 1 mg taken three times a day (for a total of 3 mg per day). Some doctors may prescribe up to 4.5 mg per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions because your dose may be different. Do not take more or less than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed when not in use. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase dizziness or drowsiness. Be careful when standing up quickly from sitting or lying down, as this medicine may cause low blood pressure and dizziness, which could lead to falls. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you. Tell all your doctors and your pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as some medicines may interact with ergoloid mesylates.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek emergency help if you experience: severe nausea or vomiting, a slow or irregular heartbeat, stuffy or blocked nose that does not go away, severe dizziness or fainting, rash or itching, chest pain, or any signs of an allergic reaction such as swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also contact your doctor if you notice no improvement in symptoms after several weeks of use.
when_it_works: This medicine works slowly. It may take several weeks to months before you or your family notice any improvement in symptoms. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor, even if you do not feel it is helping right away. Your doctor will check your progress over time to decide if the medicine is working for you.
special_populations: Older adults: This medicine is mainly used in elderly patients. Use it carefully and report any dizziness or falls to your doctor. Liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as the medicine may build up in your body. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: This medicine is generally not recommended for women who are pregnant or breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor right away if this applies to you. Children: This medicine is not intended for use in children.
